Issued at 153 AM CDT Sun Oct 25 2026

High pressure remains situated over western and central North
Dakota early this Sunday morning, with mostly clear skies and
light winds. After a cool start, we warm into the 40s north to
50s south. Abundant sunshine is expected across the area this
morning, with a slow increase in clouds across the south this
afternoon. 

Tonight, a closed upper low over the Desert Southwest lifts into
the central High Plains. High pressure over the Northern Plains
gets shunted north and east. This sets up a decent area of
isentropic upglide from the Central Plains into the Mondak 
region. The surface high to our north keeps the upglide mostly 
out of the state, except the far southwest. Light rain may 
develop in the southwest tonight. If it does, expect it may be 
later than guidance suggests (late evening, but mainly after 
midnight). Late tonight into early Monday morning, we could see 
a mix of rain and snow, or a change over to all snow. Any 
amounts are expected to be negligible. 

Better chances for precipitation will be later in the day Monday
and Monday night as the aforementioned upper low lifts into the
Dakotas. Overall there looks to be little change in the NBM 
ensemble guidance. The NBM 24 hour probability of at least an 
inch of snow, ending at 06Z Tuesday is around 30 to 60 percent 
from Bismarck southwest to Hettinger, and south to selfridge. 
This is very similar to yesterday. The medium range 
deterministic models are not as similar, compared to yesterday.
They are not as compact with the upper low lifting into south 
central ND. Yesterday the low was more closed as it lifted into 
the area, but today it's more of an open wave with a little more
shortwave energy swinging around the base of the trough, over 
southern and eastern SD. This shifts the higher qpf amounts 
farther southeast than yesterday. There's still qpf over the 
south central, but less. We'd still be in a more favored area 
for some light snow accumulations compared to the James River 
Valley, where precip here may remain mostly rain. A look at the 
latest RAP/HRRR precipitation forecasts that go out through 06Z 
Tuesday (the same ending time as the NBM 24 probability of an 
inch of snow with low to medium probabilities of an inch of snow
in south central ND) indicate pretty much all qpf remaining 
south of the state through 06Z Tuesday, with the upper low well
southeast of the medium range models. An extrapolation beyond 
06Z Tuesday, would likely keep a good portion of the south 
central dry, except maybe portions of the JRV. Needless to say, 
there's still a lot of uncertainty with this system, but the
trend for the qpf looks to be slow and farther southeast. The 
good thing is that we are looking at a pretty low impact event. 
We may still see some limited travel impacts, but for the most 
part, minimal impacts are expected at this time.

Another quick moving wave over the Pacific Northwest then swings
across the Northern Rockies and into the Northern Plains late
Tuesday through early Wednesday. This upper low tracks from
eastern Montana across northern ND. This will bring mostly low
to medium chances for light rain and snow to central and
especially northern portions of the forecast area Tuesday night.
At this time qpf amounts look to be light, and any snow
accumulations minimal.

We get a little break in the closed lows swinging through our 
area late in the work week. After Tuesday, the NBM ensemble 
temperatures show a pretty big jump, but ensemble spreads also 
increase quite a bit. Determinist models do indicate some upper 
level ridging over our area, downstream of another closed low in
the eastern Pacific. It does look like some warmer temperatures
may return mid to late week, but the extent of any warm-up 
remains a question.
